newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - the Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - the Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the global air cargo industry in the week August 26 - August 30.
**AUGUST 26**
BEIJING - A senior aviation official says only six of China's 29 airlines are profitable. He adds China is expected to place orders for about 180 new civilian planes through the year 2000.
* Xinhua news agency says China's southern city of Shenzhen handled 82.7 percent more cargo in the first half of 1996 compared with the same 1995 period.

Shen Yuankang, vice-minister of the General Administration of Civil Aviation of China says China recently voted one of the most dangerous countries in which to fly, is putting the brakes on its surging civil aviation industry to focus on safety.
KATHMANDU - Officials says Nepal and Burma signed an agreement permitting their national airlines to operate flights to each other's capital and beyond in an effort to boost tourism.
BEIJING - A senior aviation official says the long-delayed flotation of China Eastern Airlines should go ahead by the end of the year, with listings in Hong Kong and the U.S.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says it expected to be able to match 1995 earnings in the 1996 business year despite a 70 million marks fall in the first half pre-tax profit to 119 million marks.
* Lufthansa says it blamed a 37 percent slump in first-half profit mainly on price slashing by European rivals but said its full-year earnings should be stable.
KARACHI - Defence minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani says Pakistan may let three foreign airlines to fly to Lahore, the Punjab provincial capital.
TORONTO - Bombardier Aerospace president and chief operating officer Robert Brown says it has 52 firm orders for its new Global Express long-distance executive jet.

AMSTERDAM - Hans Knuvers, secretary of the Air Transport Association of the Netherlands says a working group formed to develop an integrated plan to tackle crime in the airfreight sector at Schiphol will have completed a preliminary study by end-September.
FRANKFURT - Condor Flugdienst, the charter carrier of Lufthansa says it will resume flights to Brazil and start services to Myanmar and Trinidad in its winter schedule starting November 1.
FRANKFURT - International freight forwarder Gebr. Hellmann Gmbh & Co. says it has added partners in Belgium and Egypt to its global network.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd company director, Lex Boon says its airfreight-related road haulage activities are to be brought under one management group.
BUENOS AIRES - A top official says Argentina's government chose Union Bank of Switzerland to advise it on the privatisation of the country's 57 airports.
PALO ALTO, California - Consolidated Freightways says that it plans to spin-off its long-haul, less-than-truckload units.
MELBOURNE - A spokesman says the executive chairman of Ansett Airlines, Ken Crowley, has told his managers to cut A$150 million from its annual cost base of A$3 billion over the next two years.
**AUGUST 27**
SYDNEY - Ar New Zealand budget Trans-Tasman airlines, Freedom Air international says it planned two new regular flights between Australia and New Zealand.
AUCKLAND - Aviation analysts says Air New Zealand is expected to report an annual profit towards the upper end of its own forecast range of NZ$221-234 million next week.
SHANGHAI - A senior company official says China Eastern aims to become the first Chinese airline to list shares abroad, with the listing to account for about 30 percent of its total assets.
DUBAI - China Southern Airlines says it will start a twice-weekly service to Sharjah in the UAE next month.
FRANKFURT - Belgian airlines Sabena says it foresees stable ex-Germany air cargo market rates this autumn following a slump earlier this year.
* Sabena Airlines says cargo co-operation plans for Germany with partner airline Swissair are on hold pending a strategic decision from the company's head office in Brussels.
VIENNA - Austrian Airlines spokesman says it was in co-operation talks with Singapore airlines and said it hoped to strike a deal before the start of the winter timetable at the end of October.
BUDAPEST - According to data provided to Reuters, cargo trade at Ljubljana airport in the Jan-July period decreased 15.6 percent in 1996 from 1995.
LYON - Airport authority figures show airfreight traffic handled at Lyon-Satolas airport in the first seven months of the year totalled 12,275 tonnes, up 10.5 percent on the same period in 1995.

TAIPEI - China Airlines spokesman Steve Yang says it acknowledged that is was losing money on its weekly Taipei-Johannesburg flight, but denied a local newspaper report that it would suspend the route.

NOUMEA - Airport authorities says airfreight handled at Noumea/LaTontouta airport on the French polynesian island of New Caledonian, totalled 397.4 tonnes last month, a rise of 30.6 percent on July 1995.
AMSTERDAM - Air cargo industry sources say the first half of August appears to have fought off the usual holiday slump, but the last half of the month does not seem to have been so successful.
BRUSSELS - The EC says that it had cleared the plan by BA to buy all of TAT European Airlines.
SINGAPORE - Singapore Airlines confirmed it was holding talks with Austrian Airlines on unspecified "commerical matters".
PARIS - TAT European Airline officials say they planned to meet with BA World Cargo counterparts early next month to discuss setting up a second feeder route for cargo traffic.
PARIS - Air Gabon says it made two managerial appointments following its decision to run it own French cargo office, effective September 1.
PARIS - Air France says the managing director of Air France Europe has handed in his notice of resignation.
CAIRO - Shorouk company chairman, Mahmoud el-Serafi says it may order a new Airbus 320 in the first four months of next year.
SEATTLE - Boeing says it will increase the production rate for its new 777 jet transport to seven planes per month from five in July 1997.
LONDON - Virgin Express says that objections by the Swiss authorities to the low level of its fares means it has had to call off plans to launch a new Brussels-Geneva service on September 2.
BUDAPEST - According to data provided to Reuters cargo trade at Tallinn airport in Estonia in the January-May period increaed 31.3 percent in 1996 from 1995.
FRANKFURT - Cathay Pacific says that it has cut economy class fares from Germany to Hong Kong by nearly ten percent to match lower prices from Lufthansa and Air France.
* Cathay said it is considering expanding its number of flights from Germany to ten per week from seven within the next two years.

WASHINGTON - The transportation department says the U.S. has called off "open skies" aviation talks with Britain set for this week, saying the two sides rermained too far apart for productive negotiations.
LONDON - Britain's department of transport says it was surprised by the decision by the U.S. to cancel "open skies" talks.

PARIS - An Air France execuctive says managers from Air France and its subsidiary Air France Europe will meet later this week to learn details of the group's new productivity targets and merger plans.
LONDON - BA says that it believed a breakdown of "open skies" talks between Britain and the U.S. was only temporary and a deal would be cut sooner or later.
FORT WORTH - American Airlines says it was disappointed at the postponement of "open skies" talks between the U.S. and Britain but remained hopeful that the delay was only temporary.
ATLANTA - UPS says it would nominate John Alden as vice-chairman of the board at its November board meeting.
SEATTLE - Industry analysts says Boeing is expected to use the Farnborough Air Show in England to formally launch the long-awaited stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines and Philippine Airlines announced a new partnership including the only daily-direct air services between Vancouver and Manila beginning September 19.
NEW YORK - ValuJet says it temporarily laid off 134 customer-service workers because of delays by the airline in returning to service.
NEW YORK - Analysts says American Airlines is still likely to find a European suitor even if its partnership with BA is blocked by a stalemate in the "open skies" talks between the U.S. and Britain.
